_about: The club's own facts, in one file a non-developer can edit from a phone. Everything the site asserts about the club is read from here (src/lib/content.ts); a fact that is not settled is a slot with `value: null` and the bracketed text that is waiting for a source, so the absence is explicit rather than invented. Rules this file answers to: DESIGN.md 'Copy' (state the fact, name where it came from, give a path out, carry the date; never state a frequency without a source; `[BRACKETS]` stay bracketed until a source exists), D92, D136 (no fabricated numbers), record 0010 (missing content is a designed state, never a blank and never a build failure).
_override: For a preview or a review build, copy src/content.local.example.json to src/content.local/<name>.json (gitignored, like .dev.vars) - it deep-merges over this file. Nothing tracked can turn a placeholder on: `scripts/check-content.mjs` fails any build that contains one, so a review-only state cannot reach the apex.
_sources: A claim may carry its source once, on the object that holds the group, and every claim under it inherits that source - `unsourcedSlots` in src/lib/content.ts and scripts/check-content.mjs walk ancestors, so 'the operator listed these on 2026-11-03' is written once rather than pasted nine times.

cadence.source: operator ruling, 2026-10-31, recorded in .notes/roadmap-events.md: 'Monthly is more generally correct; actual rhythm is ~every other week, occasionally skipped'
cadence.note: DESIGN.md forbids a frequency word with no source ('join us every week' survived two years). This one has a named source, which is what keeps it on the page. Set value to null and the copy falls back to naming the paths out instead of claiming a rhythm.

focus.placeholder: [what the club is taking up right now, if it wants to name one]
focus.note: Emptied 2026-11-03 on the operator's word: 'We no longer have that focus. We have no current focus at all right now.' The value it held ('Number Theory and Abstract Algebra') was pre-existing site copy with no source - `check:content` had it listed as an unsourced claim - so there was nothing to correct it against. What the club is actually pulling on is in `threads`, which is deliberately undated (see `threads._rule`). The hero renders nothing when this slot is empty rather than inventing a subject. The date-bearing label lane that used to sit under the hero is gone (D239, 2026-11-07) - the hero prints a fixed locator that cannot go stale, and the zero-event signal now lives on the schedule band, which is the surface that actually draws a calendar.

threads.source: operator, 2026-11-03, describing what the club has been discussing in its Discord channel: 'IBM Qiskit quantum computing tools, theoretical quantum physics, proof assistant languages like Lean, news in the general math field, LLMs affects on the math field, favorite math-related Youtube content, foundations of mathematics, considering the implications of arithmetic with slight changes, math exercises/puzzles that don't require expertise in a field and have interesting solutions'
threads._rule: Undated, untitled and not an archive, on purpose. Operator ruling, 2026-11-03: 'I don't want the home page to give anyone an idea that our groups interests are as narrow as what we have done historically, so I don't want to name enough specific things to give enough information to allow a pattern to emerge.' So this list carries no dates, no sequence, no book titles, no authors and no run of past topics a reader could extrapolate from. A thread that goes quiet is edited out rather than left as a record, and nothing here implies the club did something in the past or will do it in the future. Item strings are reworded for a newcomer (that is presentation, not a new claim); the operator's own words are the source above.

venues._rule: The character line is what the home page says. The names are the pool a date gets a place from, and they print next to a date, not instead of one - a visitor cannot use a list of fifteen venues, and 'meetings happen at Bauhaus Brew Labs' with no date on it is a claim about a meeting that is not scheduled (D92's defect class). Do not sort or curate this list into a pattern: it is the set of places, in the order the operator gave.

schedule._source: Corrected 2026-11-04: the earlier line here said the operator still had to provision a calendar and so 'no date on this page is knowable'. That stopped being true the day the group feed was harvested (D169) — the rows now live in data/events.json, which `src/lib/events.mjs` reads, and `upcoming` below is retired in favour of it. `src/content.json` keeps the words around the dates (the empty state), not the dates.

membership.source: the club's own Meetup group page, fetched 2026-11-03, whose member-count link reads '280 members' (https://www.meetup.com/minneapolis-mathematics-book-club/members/); the operator confirmed the figure and added that about ten of them are regular attendees
membership.note: The site used to render Math.floor(Math.random()*100+150)+'+ members' - a different community size on every request (D136, deleted). What is said here is the roster, not the attendance: it is the count on the page that carries it, dated the day it was read, with no '+' and no rounding. Do NOT publish the regular-attendee figure: ten is a fact about who shows up, it reads as a discouragement on a join page, and the operator's plan is to grow it by formalising special interest groups. Re-read the number when the page is next edited - a dated figure that has gone stale is the failure this slot's asOf exists to make visible.

photos._note: true draws measured shot-cards in the reserved photo places (PS-1, PS-3) so a preview shows the geometry a real photograph will take. It is only ever true in src/content.local.json: check:content fails a build whose HTML carries a placeholder fill.
